compactView.description:
Ask for the compact conversation view (`x-wonder-history-view:
compact`) in `threads.read` and events.

DeviceAuth.description:
The session proof a paired device gives, as for `/api/v1/events`: the
CSRF token issued with its session, and its signature over a fresh
`auth.challenge`.

signed.description:
Required from a paired device: its signature over `device.revoke`.
The local owner omits it.

body.description:
The route's JSON error body when it sent one (for example
`{"error":"idempotency_conflict"}`).

httpStatus.description: The status the route answered with, for a route refusal.

supported.description: Protocol versions this host speaks, on `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`.

EventBatchNotification.description: `events.batch` notification params; incremental events in journal order.

event.description:
A `hostEventEnvelope`; save its `hostEpoch` and `sequence` as the cursor
once it is applied.

reason.description:
`resync`: the cursor cannot be replayed (new host epoch or expired
window); read state again from `events.checkpoint`. Treat any other
reason the same way.

after.description:
Replay every event after this cursor first. Omit to receive only new
events.

batch.description:
Opt in only after initialize advertises `eventBatches`; older hosts
reject unknown fields. Omission preserves legacy single-event frames.

cursor.description: Where the stream starts: events after this cursor follow.

name.description: Empty or null goes back to the computer's own name.

HttpRequestParams.description:
One HTTP API call a phone makes through the sealed channel. It runs with
the channel's session and CSRF token through the same router and checks
as on the home network; only device API paths are served.

body.description: The JSON request body, as text.

compact.description: The compact conversation view (the HTTP API's `x-wonder-history-view`).

path.description: An `/api/v1/` path and query, percent-encoded as on the wire.

responseCompression.description:
Opt in only after initialize advertises historyCompression. Applies
only to stored history GETs; auth and arbitrary calls stay uncompressed.

HttpResponse.description: The route's answer, whatever its status.

errorCode.description: The `x-wonder-error` code a client recovers from, when the route sets one.

auth.description: Required on `/api/v1/rpc` from a paired device; omitted by the local owner.

protocolVersion.description: The major version the client speaks; this host speaks 1.

authority.description: `owner` for the local owner, `device` for a paired device.

deviceId.description: The paired device this session acts as; absent for the owner.

methods.description: Every method this host serves. Gate a feature on its method being here.

olderThanDays.description: Only files unchanged for at least this many days (default 7, at least 1).

folders.description: Orphans per preview folder (a conversation ID), largest first.

orphanedFiles.description: Files no conversation record names, older than the age limit.

recentFiles.description: Unreferenced files kept because they are newer than the age limit.

referencedFiles.description: Files a conversation record still names.

code.description: Verification text read from the phone; never echoed in a result.

route.description:
`home` makes a link on this computer's home network address, for a
phone on the same network. Omit it for the main route.

refresh.description: Check sign-in again instead of answering from the last check.

body.description: New text. Exactly one of `body`, `cancel` and `expectedTurnId`.

expectedRevision.description: Its `revision` from `threads.queue`; a changed message is a conflict.

expectedTurnId.description:
Send it now into this running turn (the thread's last turn in
`threads.read`); a turn that changed is a conflict.

label.description: The Worker's label for this computer's host key.

signed.description:
Required from a paired device: its signature over `relay.enable`
(target `/api/v1/relay/enable`, body `{"grant","label"}`, expected
state `allowed`). The local owner omits it.

allowed.description: `false` also stops the tunnel and releases the relay address.

oneOf.description: On, but not reachable right now; `detail` says why.

On, but this computer's tunnel is not running because Wonder stopped;
it reconnects at the same address when Wonder starts.

RelayView.description: What `relay.status` reports: the owner's choice and the tunnel's state.

id.description:
Absent for a notification from the client (none are defined yet; the
host ignores them).
`null` only when the request could not be read far enough to find it.

message.description: User language; safe to show as is.

historyCompression.description: Stateless compression supported by stored-history HTTP responses only.

maxInFlight.description: Requests one connection may have in flight at once.

maxRequestBytes.description: The largest request line or frame the host reads, in bytes.

apiVersion.description: The HTTP API version the routes behind the methods speak.

accessMode.description: `workspace` (default) or another access the provider offers.

accountId.description: Compatibility field: only `default` (this computer's sign-in) is accepted.

folderId.description: The Project folder to work in; default the first.

idempotencyKey.description:
A UUID made once per new thread and reused on every retry; it is the
first message's `idempotencyKey`.

accessMode.description: read_only, workspace or full_access; default and ceiling: the parent's.

folder.description:
One of the Project's folders, or a Git worktree of one (absolute path);
default: the parent's folder.

idempotencyKey.description: A UUID the client makes once per task and reuses on every retry.

maxChildren.description:
Most children the parent may have, 1–64 (default: the host's
`CUPOLA_DELEGATE_MAX_CHILDREN`, else 16).

prompt.description: The task; the child sees only this.

provider.description: Agent that runs the child: codex, claude, cursor or opencode.

branch.description: The new branch's name; made from the thread's title when absent.

before.description: The snapshot's `previousCursor`, to read the page before it.

attachmentIds.description: Files uploaded to this thread first (HTTP upload; no RPC method yet).

codexSkills.description: Skills picked in the composer, as `codexSkillSelection`.

idempotencyKey.description:
A UUID the client makes once per message and reuses on every retry of
it. With the sender's identity it is the message's identity.

projectModel.description: Send with this model; it may move a Project thread to the other provider.

consentedRunning.description: Running replies the owner agreed to pause; omit to pause any.

requestId.description: A UUID naming this update; `update.cancel` repeats it.

notificationQuestion.description: A complete nonsecret single free-text question from the actual Codex or Claude runtime. The host bounds the full display body to 382 UTF-8 bytes; richer forms omit this capability.

requestedSchema.description: The complete service form schema, never a projection that drops constraints. Limited to 64 KiB by the host.

supportsDenyMessage.description: Claude command approval accepts native denial feedback. Other providers omit or return false.

autoArchiveRule.description: Project threads archive themselves after idleDays without activity (0 = never) and, with onMerge, once their pull request merges. Pinned, working and waiting threads are skipped.

chatNotifications.description: Host-persisted per-chat policy. Default preserves existing delivery; follow also delivers child-task completions to this chat; mute suppresses chat pushes and Live Activity contributions, keeping approvals/questions in the app.

compactToolOutput.description: String tool output on compact stored history pages. output is a UTF-8 prefix of at most 2048 bytes. outputBytes counts the full sanitized UTF-8 text; outputTruncated says whether the output route must be read on expansion. Structured output is unchanged. Unstored history keeps full output.

conversationSnapshot.description: A local page of at most 100 canonical entries. Use thread.nextCursor as the next before parameter; each page has its own committed lastSequence.

historyRevision.description: Native reset epoch; pages and caches from older revisions must not be merged.

messageRecords.description: Every agent record of a message sent through T3 Code in the conversation, also outside this page, each the userMessage item (turnId, itemId) whose payload carries that message's clientId. A client labels a cached item it names the same way. Omitted when empty.

payload.description: Compact views omit payload.id and payload.text only when equal to envelope id and text. Clients read the envelope first. Stored compact string tool output follows compactToolOutput.

hostCupola.description: Cupola on the computer: what runs, the newest release known (null while unknown) and the command that updates it. A computer that sends no host is older than the app needs.

hostNameSettings.description: The computer's one name in Wonder, owned by the host: the owner's choice from the Mac app or the phone, else the computer's own name. /api/v1/host/status reports the same hostName.

systemName.description: The computer's own name, used while no name is chosen.

projectLastModel.description: The model and effort the owner last chose for one provider in a Project: starting a thread, choosing in one, or moving one to that provider.

projectRepository.description: Which repository a Project's folder belongs to, for showing the same repository on several computers together. Grouping data only: equal keys never grant access or trust.

key.description: Versioned, credential-free key from the origin remote. Compare whole keys only; keys of different versions never match.

name.description: The repository's name as its remote spells it.

subpath.description: The folder's place inside the repository, '/'-separated, empty at its top.

autoArchive.description: This Project's own rule; absent when it follows the computer's.

lastModels.description: The model last chosen in this Project, at most one per provider. A new chat without a choice of its own starts from it, ahead of the computer's default model.

repository.description: The repository holding the primary folder; absent when the folder has no comparable origin remote.

backgroundWork.description: The agent still runs background agents, commands or terminals after its reply ended. Omitted otherwise.

branch.description: The branch checked out in the thread's working folder. Omitted outside a repository or on a detached HEAD.

closedIn.description: Archived list only: the thread's home app closed it, in user language ("Settled in T3 Code", "Archived in the Claude app"). Omitted for threads archived in Cupola or Codex.

isComputerSession.description: Positive provider evidence that this chat started on a computer or is currently owned by a desktop or terminal app. Missing or false is unbadged; native identity alone is not evidence.

isSubagent.description: A T3 Code delegate_task child whose parent chat T3 Code no longer has. Children of a known parent are not listed; they appear in the parent's agent tasks. Omitted otherwise.

lastAutomationAt.description: When an automation last posted into this thread.

needsInputOnMac.description: The agent waits on the Mac itself (a permission prompt or question in its desktop app). Omitted otherwise.

reopensThere.description: Archived list only: Restore also reopens the thread in its home app when Cupola is connected there; otherwise it shows in Cupola only. Omitted otherwise.

resumesAt.description: A usage limit stopped the thread; Cupola continues it at this time (RFC 3339) unless cancelled. Omitted otherwise.

returnsAt.description: Archived list only: a thread snoozed in T3 Code returns to Chats at this time (RFC 3339).

waitingOnMacPermission.description: A macOS permission, password or download dialog is open on the Mac while this thread's turn runs; only the person at the Mac can answer it. Omitted otherwise.

providerCapabilities.description: What one provider offers through Wonder (ProviderCapabilities in crates/wonder-store/src/provider.rs). Version 1 (capabilitiesVersion); later fields are additive.

backgroundWork.description: Where the host learns that work outlived a reply, shown as a thread row's backgroundWork: terminals the runtime keeps, or tasks the session's process keeps. none: never shown.

browserUse.description: nativeChrome: Claude in Chrome when set up for Claude Code; its tool events offer the Chrome window holding Claude's tab in the computer preview.

rewind.description: Edit from here: the provider's history can be cut back to before one of the owner's messages (POST /api/v1/conversations/{conversationId}/rewind).

rewindFiles.description: A rewind can also restore files the agent edited, once the owner turns on file backups for this provider (Settings > Providers).

wonderSkills.description: Wonder's skill pack can be turned on for this provider's sessions (Settings > computer > Skills for phone).

warning.description: Chats work, but a Codex newer than Cupola was tested with, or optional features turned off, need attention.

providerUpdate.description: Whether a newer version of this provider exists, who installs it (cupola: Cupola's Claude runtime; chatgpt: ChatGPT's bundled Codex; npm or homebrew: that installer; manual: anything else), whether Cupola can run that updater (POST /api/v1/providers/{id}/update) and the last update's result.

waitsInT3Code.description: T3 Code on the computer holds this message in its thread's queue; Send now, edit and cancel go to T3 Code.

readCheckpoint.description: Authenticated host journal head. Read before fetching independent projections, atomically invalidate all cached scopes with this cursor, then replay strictly after it.

threadAutomationRun.description: The latest automation run that posted into a thread.

error.description: Why the run failed, in user language.

name.description: Null if the automation record is gone.

description: Generated by `cupola rpc --schema` from crates/wonderd/src/rpc. Do not edit; see crates/wonderd/RPC.md.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

approvals.resolve.summary: Answers an approval. Only a paired device can, with a signature over the decision.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

auth.challenge.summary: Issues the one-time challenge a paired device signs for `initialize`.

devices.forget.summary: Removes a disconnected device from the list.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

devices.rename.summary: Renames a device in the list.

devices.revoke.summary: Disconnects a device: its session ends at once.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

events.checkpoint.summary: The current event cursor. Read it before reading state, then subscribe from it, so nothing falls between the two.

events.subscribe.summary: Streams host events as `event` notifications, replaying from a cursor.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

host.name.summary: The name phones show for this computer.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

host.providers.summary: Each provider runtime on this computer and whether it is running.

host.rename.summary: Renames this computer; an empty or null name goes back to its own name.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

host.status.summary: The computer's name, platform, public origin and whether it can run agents now.

http.request.summary: Runs one of the device's own HTTP API calls inside the sealed channel, so a phone on the relay works as it does at home.

initialize.summary: Opens the session: agrees the protocol version and, on a paired device, proves the session with a signed challenge.

media.orphans.summary: Preview files no conversation names any more, older than the age limit: what media.prune would delete. Changes nothing.

media.prune.summary: Deletes the preview files media.orphans lists, and preview folders left empty.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

models.list.summary: The models each provider offers here; `isDefault` marks the one a new thread uses.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

pairing.offer.summary: Creates a pairing offer (link and code) for a new device.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

pairing.pending.summary: Devices that claimed an offer and wait for the owner's decision.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

providers.list.summary: Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode and Cursor: sign-in, models and capabilities.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

providers.reconnect.summary: Finds and checks a provider again, so it reads a new sign-in.

queue.edit.summary: Changes or cancels a queued message, or sends it now into the running turn (`expectedTurnId`).

relay.enable.summary: Starts the relay with a signed-in phone's one-time grant for this computer.

relay.set.summary: Allows the relay on this computer, or turns it off and releases its address.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

relay.status.summary: Whether this computer can be reached through Cupola's relay, and its address.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

threads.attach.summary: Gives a provider thread without a `conversationId` one, so it can be read and sent to.

threads.create.summary: Starts a thread in a Project with its first message. Idempotent per `idempotencyKey`, as `threads.send`.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

threads.delegate.summary: Starts a task as a child of a thread, like the agent tool `wonder_delegate`: the child shows in the parent as an agent task. Idempotent per `idempotencyKey`.

threads.list.summary: One page of a Project's threads, most recent first.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

threads.moveToWorktree.summary: Moves an idle thread onto a new git worktree and branch beside its repository; the thread keeps its history and carries on there.

threads.notifications.summary: The stored notification level for a chat.

threads.queue.summary: Messages waiting in a thread's queue, next first.

threads.read.summary: A thread's messages, newest page first; page back with `before`.

threads.send.summary: Sends a message. Idempotent: resending the same `idempotencyKey` and body returns the first receipt; a different body is a conflict.

threads.setNotifications.summary: Sets a chat to default, follow or mute on this computer.

update.cancel.summary: Lets the host take work again after a restart that did not happen.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

update.prepare.summary: Pauses work durably for a restart; refuses if more replies run than `consentedRunning`.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

result.description: The route's JSON body; see the guide.

update.work.summary: What a restart would interrupt: `running` replies and whether `blocksUpdate`.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

voice.dictionary.summary: The words voice mode transcribes with care.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

voice.setKey.summary: Saves the OpenAI API key voice uses.

params.description: No params: omit them, or send `{}`.

voice.status.summary: Whether voice is set up on this computer.

voice.updateDictionary.summary: Adds and removes voice dictionary words; used when the next voice session starts.

event.summary: One committed host event for a subscription, in sequence order.

events.batch.summary: Committed incremental events for an opted-in subscription, in sequence order.

events.ended.summary: A subscription stopped; `reason` says why and whether to read state again.
